html:
The Tonocoté were a farming people of the plains around the Dulce and Salado rivers in north-western Argentina, in today's Santiago del Estero province. Spanish writers called their language Tonocoté; it may have been the same as, or close to, the Lule language, but this is not settled.

They grew maize and squash on the river floodplains and lived in villages. The Spanish founded the city of Santiago del Estero in their land in 1553, the oldest Spanish city in Argentina, and the Tonocoté were divided among Spanish settlers as forced labour. Jesuit missionaries of the Society of Jesus worked among them. They gradually merged into the mestizo population; to the west lived the Diaguita.
